label: Balance-neutral good loss: A good whose loss, when suffering is prevented, leaves the balance of…
definition: A good whose loss, when suffering is prevented, leaves the balance of good and evil unchanged, rather than improving it. Rowe p.336 n.3 suggests that such a cost may also exempt the being from prevention. The refinement therefore weakens the necessary permission constraint and strengthens the factual gratuitous-suffering premise. It does not make an indifferent balance sufficient to justify permission.
